passages.text: “I am the true vine, and My Father is the keeper of the vineyard.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus says, "I am the true vine."
My Father is the keeper of the vineyard.
My Father cares for the vine.
My Father watches over the vineyard.
passages.original: Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἄμπελος ἡ ἀληθινή καὶ ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ γεωργός ἐστιν

passages.text: He cuts off every branch in Me that bears no fruit, and every branch that does bear fruit, He prunes to make it even more fruitful.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the true vine.
God the Father is the keeper of the vineyard.
God removes every branch in Jesus that does not bear fruit.
God prunes every branch that bears fruit.
God prunes fruitful branches so they will bear more fruit.
passages.original: πᾶν κλῆμα ἐν ἐμοὶ μὴ φέρον καρπὸν αἴρει αὐτό καὶ πᾶν τὸ καρπὸν φέρον καθαίρει αὐτὸ ἵνα καρπὸν πλείονα φέρῃ

passages.text: You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nJesus said, “You are already clean.\r\nYou are clean because of the word I have spoken to you.”
passages.original: ἤδη ὑμεῖς καθαροί ἐστε διὰ τὸν λόγον ὃν λελάληκα ὑμῖν

passages.text: Remain in Me, and I will remain in you. Just as no branch can bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus tells them to remain in Him.
He promises that He will remain in them.
A branch cannot bear fruit by itself.
A branch must remain in the vine to bear fruit.
In the same way, you cannot bear fruit by yourselves.
You must remain in Jesus to bear fruit.
passages.original: μείνατε ἐν ἐμοί κἀγὼ ἐν ὑμῖν καθὼς τὸ κλῆμα οὐ δύναται καρπὸν φέρειν ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ ἐὰν μὴ μένῃ ἐν τῇ ἀμπέλῳ οὕτως οὐδὲ ὑμεῖς ἐὰν μὴ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένητε

passages.text: I am the vine and you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, will bear much fruit. For apart from Me you can do nothing.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus says, "I am the vine."
You are the branches.
If anyone remains in Me, and I remain in him, he will bear much fruit.
Without Me, you can do nothing.
passages.original: Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἄμπελος ὑμεῖς τὰ κλήματα ὁ μένων ἐν ἐμοὶ κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ οὗτος φέρει καρπὸν πολύν ὅτι χωρὶς ἐμοῦ οὐ δύνασθε ποιεῖν οὐδέν

passages.text: If anyone does not remain in Me, he is like a branch that is thrown away and withers. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus is the vine.
His disciples are the branches.
If a person does not remain in Jesus, that person is like a branch.
People throw away this branch.
The branch dries up.
People gather these dry branches.
They throw the branches into the fire.
The branches burn.
passages.original: ἐὰν μή τις μένῃ ἐν ἐμοί ἐβλήθη ἔξω ὡς τὸ κλῆμα καὶ ἐξηράνθη καὶ συνάγουσιν αὐτὰ καὶ εἰς τὸ πῦρ βάλλουσιν καὶ καίεται

passages.text: If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus is the vine.
His disciples are the branches.
If you remain in Jesus, you stay connected to Him.
If Jesus' words remain in you, you keep His teachings in your heart.
If you remain in Jesus and His words remain in you, you can ask for anything you wish.
God will do it for you.
passages.original: ἐὰν μείνητε ἐν ἐμοὶ καὶ τὰ ῥήματά μου ἐν ὑμῖν μείνῃ ὃ ἐὰν θέλητε αἰτήσασθε καὶ γενήσεται ὑμῖν

passages.text: This is to My Father’s glory, that you bear much fruit, proving yourselves to be My disciples.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
God is the Father of Jesus.
God receives glory when you bear much fruit.
You bear much fruit by living as Jesus teaches.
When you bear much fruit, you show that you are Jesus’ disciples.
passages.original: ἐν τούτῳ ἐδοξάσθη ὁ Πατήρ μου ἵνα καρπὸν πολὺν φέρητε καὶ γένησθε ἐμοὶ μαθηταί

passages.text: As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you. Remain in My love.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
The Father loved Jesus.
Jesus loved His disciples in the same way.
Jesus tells His disciples to remain in His love.
passages.original: Καθὼς ἠγάπησέν με ὁ Πατήρ κἀγὼ ὑμᾶς ἠγάπησα μείνατε ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ τῇ ἐμῇ

passages.text: If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
Jesus gives commandments to His disciples.
If you keep Jesus’ commandments, you remain in Jesus’ love.
Jesus has kept His Father’s commandments.
Jesus remains in His Father’s love.
passages.original: ἐὰν τὰς ἐντολάς μου τηρήσητε μενεῖτε ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ μου καθὼς ἐγὼ τοῦ Πατρός μου τὰς ἐντολὰς τετήρηκα καὶ μένω αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ

passages.text: I have told you these things so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
\r\nJesus told them important things.
\r\nHe wanted His own joy to be in them.
\r\nHe wanted their joy to be full.
passages.original: Ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ἡ ἐμὴ ἐν ὑμῖν ᾖ καὶ ἡ χαρὰ ὑμῶν πληρωθῇ

passages.text: This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus gives a commandment.
He says, "This is My commandment."
He commands, "Love one another."
He says, "Love one another as I have loved you."
Jesus has shown love to His disciples.
He wants His disciples to love each other in the same way.
passages.original: Αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐντολὴ ἡ ἐμὴ ἵνα ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους καθὼς ἠγάπησα ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus teaches about love.
No one has greater love than this.
A person shows the greatest love by laying down his life for his friends.
passages.original: μείζονα ταύτης ἀγάπην οὐδεὶς ἔχει ἵνα τις τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ θῇ ὑπὲρ τῶν φίλων αὐτοῦ

passages.text: You are My friends if you do what I command you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
Jesus calls them His friends.
They are His friends if they do what He commands.
Jesus gives commands to them.
Obeying His commands shows they are His friends.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς φίλοι μού ἐστε ἐὰν ποιῆτε ἃ ἐγὼ ἐντέλλομαι ὑμῖν

passages.text: No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not understand what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because everything I have learned from My Father I have made known to you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, "I do not call you servants anymore."
A servant does not know what his master is doing.
I have called you friends.
I have told you everything I heard from My Father.
I have made all these things known to you.
passages.original: οὐκέτι λέγω ὑμᾶς δούλους ὅτι ὁ δοῦλος οὐκ οἶδεν τί ποιεῖ αὐτοῦ ὁ κύριος ὑμᾶς δὲ εἴρηκα φίλους ὅτι πάντα ἃ ἤκουσα παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός μου ἐγνώρισα ὑμῖν

passages.text: You did not choose Me, but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit—fruit that will remain—so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, "You did not choose Me."
"I chose you."
"I appointed you."
I want you to go.
I want you to bear fruit.
Your fruit will last.
When you ask the Father in My name, He will give it to you.
passages.original: οὐχ ὑμεῖς με ἐξελέξασθε ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ ἐξελεξάμην ὑμᾶς καὶ ἔθηκα ὑμᾶς ἵνα ὑμεῖς ὑπάγητε καὶ καρπὸν φέρητε καὶ ὁ καρπὸς ὑμῶν μένῃ ἵνα ὅ¦τι ἂν αἰτήσητε τὸν Πατέρα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου δῷ ὑμῖν

passages.text: This is My command to you: Love one another.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nJesus gave them a command.\r\nHe said, "Love one another."
passages.original: ταῦτα ἐντέλλομαι ὑμῖν ἵνα ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους

passages.text: If the world hates you, understand that it hated Me first.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of God.
If the world hates you, know this.
The world hated Me before it hated you.
passages.original: Εἰ ὁ κόσμος ὑμᾶς μισεῖ γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐμὲ πρῶτον ὑμῶν μεμίσηκεν

passages.text: If you were of the world, it would love you as its own. Instead, the world hates you, because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus had chosen His disciples out of the world.
The disciples do not belong to the world.
If the disciples belonged to the world, the world would love them as its own.
But the disciples do not belong to the world.
Because of this, the world hates the disciples.
passages.original: εἰ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἦτε ὁ κόσμος ἂν τὸ ἴδιον ἐφίλει ὅτι δὲ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου οὐκ ἐστέ ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ ἐξελεξάμην ὑμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου διὰ τοῦτο μισεῖ ὑμᾶς ὁ κόσμος

passages.text: Remember the word that I spoke to you: ‘No servant is greater than his master.’ If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well; if they kept My word, they will keep yours as well.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, "No servant is greater than his master."
Remember this word.
People persecuted Me.
They will persecute you also.
Some people kept My word.
They will keep your word also.
passages.original: Μνημονεύετε τοῦ λόγου οὗ ἐγὼ εἶπον ὑμῖν Οὐκ ἔστιν δοῦλος μείζων τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ εἰ ἐμὲ ἐδίωξαν καὶ ὑμᾶς διώξουσιν εἰ τὸν λόγον μου ἐτήρησαν καὶ τὸν ὑμέτερον τηρήσουσιν

passages.text: But they will treat you like this because of My name, since they do not know the One who sent Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “They will do all these things to you because of My name.”
They do not know the One who sent Me.
This is why they will treat you this way.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ταῦτα πάντα ποιήσουσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου ὅτι οὐκ οἴδασιν τὸν πέμψαντά με

passages.text: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin. Now, however, they have no excuse for their sin.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus came to the people.
Jesus spoke to them.
If Jesus had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin.
Now they have heard Jesus.
Now they have no excuse for their sin.
passages.original: εἰ μὴ ἦλθον καὶ ἐλάλησα αὐτοῖς ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ εἴχοσαν νῦν δὲ πρόφασιν οὐκ ἔχουσιν περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν

passages.text: Whoever hates Me hates My Father as well.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of God.
God is the Father who sent Jesus.
Anyone who hates Jesus also hates God the Father.
Hating Jesus means hating His Father too.
passages.original: Ὁ ἐμὲ μισῶν καὶ τὸν Πατέρα μου μισεῖ

passages.text: If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not be guilty of sin; but now they have seen and hated both Me and My Father.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus did works among them.
No one else did these works.
If Jesus had not done these works among them, they would not be guilty of sin.
Now they have seen these works.
Now they have hated Jesus.
Now they have hated the Father also.
passages.original: εἰ τὰ ἔργα μὴ ἐποίησα ἐν αὐτοῖς ἃ οὐδεὶς ἄλλος ἐποίησεν ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ εἴχοσαν νῦν δὲ καὶ ἑωράκασιν καὶ μεμισήκασιν καὶ ἐμὲ καὶ τὸν Πατέρα μου

passages.text: But this is to fulfill what is written in their Law: ‘They hated Me without reason.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks about Himself.
Jesus says some people hate Him.
Their Law contains a written word.
This word says, “They hated Me without reason.”
Their hatred fulfills this word in their Law.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ἵνα πληρωθῇ ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ αὐτῶν γεγραμμένος ὅτι Ἐμίσησάν με δωρεάν

passages.text: When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father—He will testify about Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said He would send the Advocate to them.
The Advocate is the Spirit of truth.
The Spirit of truth comes from the Father.
The Advocate will come from the Father.
The Advocate will testify about Jesus.
passages.original: Ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ Παράκλητος ὃν ἐγὼ πέμψω ὑμῖν παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός τὸ Πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας ὃ παρὰ τοῦ Πατρὸς ἐκπορεύεται ἐκεῖνος μαρτυρήσει περὶ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: And you also must testify, because you have been with Me from the beginning.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, "You must testify about Me."
You have been with Me from the beginning.
You know Me and My works.
You can speak about what you have seen and heard.
passages.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς δὲ μαρτυρεῖτε ὅτι ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστε
